messages:
Anya: Quick heads-up — PMs want a single operational dashboard that ties routing/quota rollouts to surface-level customer metrics. We need runtime + infra to agree on a small telemetry contract (request id, trace id, route/model/variant tags, sampling). Who can own the contract and a minimal example?
Mike: I can help on the dashboard side but need the exact fields. Do we have a stable header for request_id today?
Sasha: runtime currently emits a span tag `req.id` and `trace.id` for traced requests, but the request header isn't always propagated from edge -> runtime unless infra sets passthrough. Sampling is ~1% global right now.
Lucas: infra: we do normalize headers at the LB. By default some internal proxies drop `X-Request-Id`. We can enable passthrough and set `proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $request_id;` in the nginx layer. We'll open a config PR.
Aly (PM): For the dashboard we care about: p50/p95 latency by route, error rate, request volume, % of requests traced, and traffic split by rollout variant. Also want a metric for "requests with request_id" so we know coverage.
Anya: Here's a suggested telemetry contract snippet — minimal and machine-readable so console can rely on it:
```
{
  "trace_name": "redwood.request",
  "fields": ["request_id", "trace_id", "route", "model", "variant", "status_code", "latency_ms"],
  "required": ["request_id", "route", "latency_ms"]
}
```
Sasha: I like that. Implementation notes: runtime will emit `trace_name=redwood.request` and include those tags on spans when sampled. We'll also add a fast path to inject `request_id` into access logs for non-sampled requests.
Mike: For linking logs <-> traces, if access logs include `request_id` and we store that in our logging pipeline, dashboards can join logs <-> traces. Do we have a standard field name for logs? `req_id` vs `request_id`?
Lucas: Let's standardize on `request_id` (snake_case) across infra/runtime/logs. I'll update the access_log_format in the nginx template: `access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main;` where main includes `$request_id` and `$trace_id`.
Sasha: Sampling policy proposal (can be added to runtime config):
```yaml
tracing:
  default_rate: 0.01   # 1% of traffic
  overrides:
    - match: "/api/canary/*"
      rate: 0.2        # 20% for canary routes
    - match: "/admin/*"
      rate: 1.0        # always sample admin traffic
```
We can make rules pluggable by route or header.
Aly (PM): That looks good. Can we also emit a per-route `trace_coverage` metric (count_traced / count_total) so the dashboard shows coverage?
Anya: Yes — runtime should emit two counters per route: `requests_total{route=..}` and `requests_traced{route=..}`. Console can calculate `trace_coverage = requests_traced / requests_total`.
Mike: Who's picking up the console widgets? I can prototype if infra/runtime provide the fields and a small test dataset. ETA for that?
Lucas: I'll file infra PR to enable header passthrough + access log injection today, target staging by EOD tomorrow. PR link will be posted here.
Sasha: I'll land runtime changes to tag spans and emit the two counters within the next 3 days. Will post integration test that asserts `request_id` appears in access logs for non-sampled requests.
Aly (PM): Owners: runtime -> Sasha, infra -> Lucas, console/dashboard prototype -> Mike, product acceptance -> Aly. If anyone disagrees, speak now.
Anya: Sounds good. One more UX ask: when rollouts are configured in console, show expected trace coverage and a note when coverage < 5% (so PMs know instrumentation is low).
Mike: Good call — I'll add a warning banner if `trace_coverage < 0.05`.
infra-bot: CI: header-proxy config PR #452 passed staging checks (integration tests for header passthrough). :white_check_mark:
Sasha: Nice. After infra PR merges I'll run the runtime integration test against staging and then we can flip the dashboard to read staging metrics.
Aly (PM): Great progress, thank you all. Can we have a short sync tomorrow at 11am to confirm PRs and dashboard prototype? :calendar: 
Anya: Yep — 11am works. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
